newsitem.title: JAPAN: FTC OK's merger of Mitsui Petchem, Mitsui Toatsu.
newsitem.headline: FTC OK's merger of Mitsui Petchem, Mitsui Toatsu.

text.p: Japan's Fair Trade Commission (FTC) said on Wednesday it had approved a merger scheduled for this October between two major Japanese chemical makers, even though the new firm would hold a large market share in some products.
The two firms are Mitsui Petrochemical Industries Ltd and Mitsui Toatsu Chemicals Inc.
The two companies announced last October that they planned to merge to become Mitsui Chemicals Inc, creating the second-largest chemical manufacturer in Japan after Mitsubishi Chemical Corp.

The FTC, Japan's anti-monopoly watchdog, said in a statement that the high market shares the new firm was expected to command in several chemical products would not hinder free competition in the domestic market.
It was estimated that the new firm would have a combined market share of 57.3 percent for phenol and 26.2 percent for polypropylene.
Phenol is used as feedstock for agricultural chemicals and polypropylene is used to manufacture a wide variety of parts for cars and electrical appliances.
The dominant phenol share will not pose a threat of limited competition in the market as end-users can easily turn to imports as an alternative, the FTC said.

As for polypropylene, competition was expected to be maintained as another chemical firm also holds a market share of more than 20 percent, while several companies have market shares exceeding 10 percent, the commission said.
